lens: temporal identity governance, policy immutability, human override authority, and privacy
strengths: Every new identity confirmation resolves one effective policy at confirmation time and snapshots its version, final deadline, validity basis, and optional human override reason on the handle.
The same policy snapshot is copied into immutable lifecycle history and privacy-safe audit metadata rather than inferred later from current configuration.
Default intervals live in a versioned policy document, while a custom deadline fails closed unless the recruiter supplies a bounded visible reason.
A reason without a custom deadline also fails closed, preventing meaningless or misleading override metadata.
The policy maximum bounds both defaults and human overrides; an invalid or unavailable policy stops confirmation instead of falling back silently.
Published policy content, version, effective start, and maximum cannot be edited or deleted. The database permits only one-way retirement followed by a non-overlapping successor.
A rolled-back v2 transition directly proves that new confirmations can use v2 while existing v1 policy versions and exact deadlines remain unchanged.
The human override basis and reason appear in durable relationship Agent history so the decision remains understandable after reload.
Raw email, WeChat, and phone values remain absent from the identity index, lifecycle projection, audit projection, and Agent history.
The slice performs no automatic person decision or consequential external write.
missing_evidence: Field calibration of each default interval using observed corrections, reconfirmations, and issuer-specific identifier behavior.
A privileged production deployment proof showing that only migration governance can retire or add policies.
Concurrent policy retirement and confirmation tests at the exact effective-time boundary.
Exact Web and iOS review copy for a human override, including accessibility and later explanation.
open_questions: Should source-native identifiers name an issuer-specific policy instead of sharing one generic 180-day interval?
Which roles, if any, may set a custom identity deadline, and should an extension require stronger evidence than a shorter interval?
